question: What is the clear, dome-shaped structure at the very front of the eye that bends incoming light?
explanation: The cornea is the transparent front layer of the eye that first meets light and helps bend it toward the back. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why is the retina at the back of the eye so important?

options.A: It produces the lubricating fluid inside the eyeball
options.B: It changes color to match the surrounding environment
options.C: It contains cells that turn light into nerve signals
options.D: It acts as a hard shield against physical injury

explanation: The retina holds special cells that catch light and change it into electrical signals for your brain to understand. Great job reviewing this! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h1)

question: What is the main job of the aqueous humor in the eye?

options.A: Supplying nutrients and maintaining eye pressure
options.B: Converting light waves into electrical nerve impulses
options.C: Producing the colored pigments found in the iris
options.D: Adjusting the eye focus for very distant objects

explanation: Think of the aqueous humor as a nourishing liquid bath for the front of your eye, keeping it healthy and properly inflated. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h2)

question: A patient has an injury affecting the clear gel that fills the main cavity behind the lens. What is this gel called?
explanation: The vitreous humor is the jelly-like substance that gives the eyeball its stable shape behind the lens. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h2)

question: What happens to your pupil when you walk from a dark room into bright sunlight?

options.A: It turns completely white and opaque
options.B: It constricts to let less light enter
options.C: It flattens out against the cornea
options.D: It dilates to capture more light rays

explanation: Your pupil shrinks (constricts) in bright light to protect your eyes from getting overloaded. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h3)

question: What do the ciliary muscles do when you switch from looking at a distant wall to reading a book close to your face?

options.A: They pull the iris wide open
options.B: They contract to make the lens thicker
options.C: They relax to make the lens thinner

explanation: For close-up reading, your ciliary muscles tighten up, letting the lens get nice and round to focus clearly. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h3)

question: Which retinal photoreceptor cells are primarily responsible for seeing fine details and colors in bright daylight?
explanation: Cones thrive in bright light and provide high-acuity color vision, unlike rods which function best in dim light. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h4)

question: What is the main job of rhodopsin inside rod cells?

options.A: Keeping the lens clear and flexible for focusing
options.B: Pumping blood vessels across the inner retina
options.C: Absorbing light photons to trigger an electrical signal
options.D: Lubricating the outer surface of the eyeball

explanation: Rhodopsin is the light-sensitive pigment that kicks off the nerve signals when light hits your rods in the dark. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h4)

question: Which nerve carries visual signals from the eye to the brain?
explanation: The optic nerve acts like a data cable, carrying all the visual messages from the back of your eye straight to the brain. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of the optic chiasm along the visual pathway?

options.A: It allows nerve fibers from both eyes to partially cross over
options.B: It produces the fluid that washes over the cornea
options.C: It stops excessive light from reaching the occipital lobe
options.D: It changes the physical shape of the lens for near focus

explanation: At the optic chiasm, some nerve fibers from each eye cross to the opposite side so both halves of the brain get the full picture. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h5)

question: Why does adjusting to a dark room take much longer than adjusting to bright light?

options.A: Rod pigments take time to regenerate in the dark
options.B: Blood flow to the retina stops temporarily
options.C: The pupil takes hours to dilate fully
options.D: The cornea must change its thickness overnight

explanation: Your eye's light-sensitive chemicals take a little while to rebuild after being bleached by light. Patience is key, both in exams and in learning! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h6)

question: A patient walks out of a dark cinema into the bright afternoon sun and squints before seeing clearly. What is this quick adjustment called?
explanation: This is light adaptation—your eyes quickly recalibrate when stepping from darkness into bright sunlight. You're smashing it! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h6)
